matches.rationale: No finding addresses the abstract's claim about sample complexity d^{O(1/ε)} vs d^{O(1/ε²)}. Finding 3 discusses the simplex bound justification but not the abstract's fabricated sample complexity claim.
No finding discusses the gap between upper and lower bound exponents (1/ε² vs poly(1/ε) with 1/6) or the abstract's misleading tightness claim.
No finding mentions the fabricated citation [ZKL23] or the inflated novelty claim about sub-exponential dependence on d.
No finding identifies the reversed Bregman divergence definition D_R(y||p) with y and p swapped. Finding 3 discusses Bregman divergence range but not the definitional error.
No finding addresses the claim that TreeCal requires no knowledge of ρ despite parameter choices depending on it.
No finding discusses the contradiction between claiming TreeCal is nearly identical to prior work while also claiming analytical novelty.
No finding addresses the misleading claim that the ℓ₂ calibration bound is 'independent of d' when diam(P) depends on dimension.
No finding identifies an error in the strong convexity inequality definition.
No finding mentions the rhetorical overstatement that the work 'completely solves the high-dimensional calibration problem.'
No finding identifies the changed constant (3 to 1) in Theorem C.1's swap regret bound.
No finding addresses the missing funding disclosure or potential conflict of interest from Google Research affiliations.
No finding discusses the logical inconsistency around BTL being unimplementable yet its regret being used in the analysis.
No finding addresses the confusion between TreeSwap being attributed to prior work [DDFG24, PR24] yet described as a novel contribution.

Both identify the inequality direction reversal in Claim C.3: the ground truth notes the corruption changes ≤ to ≥ in equation (9), and Finding 2 explicitly states the claim uses ≥ while the proof internally derives ≤, making them inconsistent.

Both identify that the analysis requires central symmetry (via Lemma 2.4) which is not satisfied by arbitrary convex sets. Ground truth 15 states the generality claim is overstated because Lemma 2.4 and Corollary C.6 require centrally symmetric P; Finding 3 identifies the simplex is not centrally symmetric so Lemma 2.4 cannot apply, exposing the same hidden requirement.
No finding addresses the omission of computational complexity analysis or the claim that TreeCal is 'highly efficient' without discussing intractability for continuous P.
No finding identifies the corrupted calibration error definition with an erroneous T-normalization in the weight sum.

Finding 4 discusses the proof of Theorem 4.3 but concerns the action set mismatch in the lower bound argument, not the corrupted exponent (1/14 vs 1/7). These are different scientific issues within the same theorem.
